newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mistake to launch EMU without Italy -BOF's Gerard.
newsitem.headline: Mistake to launch EMU without Italy -BOF's Gerard.

text.p: Jean-Pierre Gerard, a member of Bank of France's monetary policy council, said it would be extremely damaging to launch the European monetary union without Italy.
"It would be a mistake to create the euro without them," Gerard was quoted as telling Le Monde in an interview on Thursday.
"If Italy meets the Maastricht criteria, there is no reason for it not to participate in the single currency -- that's the answer on the technical side," he was quoted as saying.
"There is a more political response. It would be extremely damaging to take such a crucial step in Europe without Italy, who has been with us since the (EU founding) Treaty of Rome."

"There is a problem of loyalty to history. They wanted the construction of Europe, with the Germans and the French. It would be a mistake to create the euro without them," Gerard, who is seen as one of a minority of monetary policy doves in the independent French central bank, was quoted as saying.
